messages:
maria-sec: :rotating_light: saw multiple reports of an exploit in the wild targeting libpq connection string parsing — can we triage? link: https://security-advisories.example.org/CVE-2026-9999
jon-eng: ugh, is this the authentication-bypass one that ignores password params?
sam-infra: yes, vendor advisory says malformed connstr can bypass auth on certain client versions (libpq 1.2.0 - 1.3.4)
lee-prodsec: CVSS prelim 9.0 per advisory. Exploit PoC circulating. We need immediate mitigations for hosted endpoints and a patch plan for Dedicated/Private customers.
ops-oncall: oncall here — I can schedule emergency deploys for hosted in the next 30m.
ops-bot: Incident created: SECURITY-2026-042 — Emergency triage for CVE-2026-9999 (libpq connstr auth bypass). https://redwood-incidents/SEC-2026-042
maria-sec: action list: 1) quick mitigation for hosted (WAF rule + kill feature flag) 2) patch runtime images to libpq 1.3.5+ and roll 3) notify Dedicated customers and provide patch/mitigation steps 4) draft public advisory + status page update 5) coordinate legal/comms
jon-eng: short-term mitigation that works for us: enforce server-side auth enforcement (reject connstrings with empty password fields) and block known exploit UA patterns at edge. I can push a middleware check to runtime in a PR.
sam-infra: adding an nginx WAF rule now to block connstrings containing "password=" with empty value and requests with suspicious payload size. Applying as emergency rule to hosted region us-west-2 first.
lee-prodsec: also disable automatic credential discovery for our KMS credential helper in the runtime until we ship patched libpq; we saw exploit combining connstr trick with credential fallback. Can we toggle via FF?
jon-eng: yes, config flag redwood.runtime.kms_auto_try = false — I’ll prepare a hotfix that flips it for hosted and Dedicated control plane.
ops-oncall: deploying WAF rule to us-west-2 -> applied. Monitoring logs for blocked hits.
ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime-middleware v2026.03.18-hotfix to hosted-production-us-west-2 by jon-eng
jon-eng: pushed PR #4123 with the connstr validation and flag flip. Test plan in PR description. Please review fast.
nick-sre: rolling canary of patched runtime to 5% in us-west-2. Observability hooked into token-latency and error-rate dashboards.
emma-support: prepping customer advisory draft for Support/Success to use for Dedicated and Private customers — will need instructions for manual KMS config and image roll.
claudia-legal: heads up — we should avoid wording that assigns blame. Provide actionable mitigations and an ETA for full patch. I’ll review advisory language.
lee-prodsec: immediate prioritization: Hosted: P1 (deploy now). Dedicated: P1 (notify & offer coordinated patch window). Private/on-prem: P2 (we’ll publish backport and guidance). Backport to 1.10.x and 1.11.x branches.
jon-eng: target builds: libpq 1.3.5 (vendor fix) and a patched runtime build v2026.03.18. Backports started for 1.10.x and 1.11.x.
sam-infra: build images with patched libpq and push to registry; we'll tag hosted images with rtk-patch-0318 and push to canary. Expected build complete in 22m.
ops-bot: Image build success: registry.redwood/rtk:2026.03.18-patch (sha256:abcd1234)
ops-oncall: starting canary rollout of patched image to us-west-2 (10% traffic)
nick-sre: monitoring — no regressions in cpu/mem so far. Latency unchanged.
jon-eng: once canary stable for 15m, we do progressive rollout to 100% in us-west then global.
lee-prodsec: mitigation checklist for Dedicated/Private customers:
- If you are on Managed Dedicated, we can schedule a live patch during your maintenance window. Contact success@redwood.ai with your preferred window.
- For Private/on-prem, disable kms_auto_try and follow our manual upgrade guide to libpq 1.3.5. Provide backport patches for runtime versions 1.10.x and 1.11.x.
Include the curl snippet to detect exploit attempts:
```
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"conn_str":"host=... user=... password=\"\""}' \
  https://your-hosted-endpoint/api/v1/query
```
If the endpoint returns 200 for that payload, treat as vulnerable.

emma-support: drafted email template for customers (short):
"We’re investigating CVE-2026-9999 affecting libpq client parsing. Hosted customers: mitigations applied; we're rolling a full patch. Dedicated/Private: review attached mitigation steps and contact support to schedule patching."

claudia-legal: reviewed — OK with edits, send to comms for final copy.
maria-sec: risk notes: exploit actively used for data-exfil attempts in small set of customers; no evidence of mass compromise yet. Prioritize customers with high-volume DB connections and KMS-integrated runtimes.
jon-eng: PR merged, full rollout started to all hosted regions.
ops-bot: Rollout complete: 100% hosted regions updated.
ops-oncall: all hosted regions patched. WAF rules remain for extra protection for 72h.
lee-prodsec: please open support tickets for each Dedicated customer we proactively patch and capture confirmation. Emma, can you coordinate?
emma-support: will create tracker and notify customers in batches — first wave sent to 8 Dedicated customers with high risk.
nick-sre: postmortem timeline entry: initial triage, WAF + flag mitigation, canary, global rollout, customer comms. We should prepare an eval to detect regressions for 7 days.
maria-sec: follow-ups: (1) Confirm KMS credential logs for any abnormal access (2) Full forensics on impacted customer snapshots (3) Advisory publish draft ready by EOD.
jon-eng: will push backport patches to 1.10.x and 1.11.x tonight.
lee-prodsec: thanks team. Any objections to the comms/patch plan? If none, we'll close incident as mitigated and move to monitoring/forensics.
ops-oncall: no objections. Marking incident as mitigated in status page.
ops-bot: Incident updated: STATUS -> Mitigated. Next step: Forensics + Postmortem (owner: maria-sec).
maria-sec: assigning postmortem and timeline to myself. Will assemble notes and detection rules for the threat intel feed. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
